subject: Action items: streaming p95 spikes & PoC data request
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Shah <ravi@orion-health.ai>, Orion Health SRE <sre@orion-health.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Action items: streaming p95 spikes & PoC data request

Hi Ravi / Orion SRE team —

Thanks again for a focused call this morning. Below is a concise recap of what we heard from your side, plus the next steps we discussed. I kept the asks separated so we can track ownership.

What you described (pain points)
- Realtime transcript & summarization API is seeing large p95 latency spikes during concurrent live sessions (reported p95 ~1.1–1.4s during peak).
- Streaming UX: customers see a delayed first-byte for streaming responses ~200–400ms in many cases; sometimes the stream stalls mid-response.
- Concurrency: workload pattern has many short-lived sessions (avg 6–12 tokens per turn) but traffic bursts up to ~300 concurrent streams.
- Current stack: Triton-based model serving (v2.17) on dedicated GPU pool; no prefix KV caching; batching is at inference runtime but is conservative to avoid tail latencies.

Your success criteria we captured
- P95 end-to-end generation latency <= 500ms for common prompts.
- Streaming first-byte (time-to-first-chunk) <= 200ms for 90% of requests.
- Sustain 200 concurrent streaming sessions without observable p95 regressions.

Immediate asks / agreed next steps
1) Data handoff (Action: Orion SRE) — share a 30-minute window of production traces + a 1% sample of request payloads (tokenized inputs OK) and a short timeline of when spikes occurred. Helps us reproduce and correlate with cache misses or load imbalance.
2) Redwood PoC (Action: Ben / Marissa) — run a scoped PoC in your staging with a small fleet of dedicated nodes; aim to show p95 improvements via KV prefix caching + tuned batching. We can target a 2-week PoC.
3) Live demo (Action: Ben) — schedule a short demo (30–45m) to show streaming optimizations and how fallback routing to a smaller model variant could reduce cost during sustained bursts.
4) Acceptance criteria doc (Action: Karthik) — draft a short MOP with target SLOs and test plan; we agreed to iterate once we see traces.

Attachments: I attached a one-page proposed MOP that outlines the PoC scope and the sample metrics we plan to collect (orion_mop_v1.pdf) and a screenshot of the p95 graph style we use (p95-graphs.png).

Proposed times for the demo: Wed/Tue late-morning PST or Thu early afternoon PST. Share what works and we’ll send a calendar invite.

If you’re comfortable, share a short read-only SRE contact or bucket for traces and we’ll pull the artifacts directly. Otherwise reply with attachments.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this reproducible.

—
Ben Carter

Subject: Re: Action items: streaming p95 spikes & PoC data request

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few points from our SRE side:
- We did see p95 jump to ~1.3s around 08:32 and 09:05 PST yesterday; CPU and GPU utilization didn’t spike correspondingly, which suggests cache misses / KV cold paths or queuing at Triton.
- Streaming stalls tend to coincide with model reloads after nightly *auto-update* windows — we think we can disable auto-updates for the PoC window.

We’ll upload a 30m trace bundle and a small sample payload set to a read-only bucket (link below) by EOD tomorrow. The traces include span-level timings and our client-side TTFB measurements.

We’re available for the demo on Wed 08/19 at 10:00 AM PST or Thu 08/20 at 13:00 PST — Wed 10:00 is preferred. Please send an invite.

Attaching the compressed traces I pulled from staging (latency-traces-20260816.zip) — contains traces.json and client-ttfb.csv.

Ravi
Senior Product Manager | Orion Health
ravi@orion-health.ai
